content:
Former Republican National Committee Chair Ronna McDaniel called out the Republican Party on Tuesday for spending hundreds of millions of dollars on Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton in the midterms — and predicted that Democrats will “probably” win back the House.

McDaniel made her case on CBS News after “The Takeout” host Major Garrett asked what she believes will happen in the November elections, noting that the Democrats won back the House in 2018 and had “swept” both the House and Senate during the 2006 midterms.

“I obviously was there in 2018,” said McDaniel. “It was a very tough midterm. The House map has shrunk because of redistricting and because of what the Trump administration did in the first year, changing maps in Texas and other states. So there’s less House seats at play.”

She continued, “So I don’t think you’re gonna see a 50-seat wave.”

McDaniel, who was RNC chair from 2017 to 2024, said this is “just not possible anymore.” She also noted that the GOP has “so much more money” today, however, and that the effect of having “$180 million pour into Texas and some of these states” remains unclear.

“I will also say, in 2018 we did pick up Senate seats, which was unusual in a midterm,” she said. “And I think Republicans could keep the Senate, but it is a tough environment out there.”

Garrett noted that this wasn’t the case just six months ago when “most Republicans” viewed the midterms electoral map as an easy “layup,” prompting McDaniel to agree — and note that President Donald Trump hasn’t been campaigning across the country for nothing.

“The fact that we’re talking about Kansas, the fact that the president’s been in South Carolina and Mississippi, I know for a fact you’re not in these states unless there’s a data point that’s driving him to spend time in those states,” she said. “How many times has he been to Texas?”

Trump has personally campaigned for Paxton on numerous occasions, with at least three visits to Texas in October alone, despite the former state attorney general’s many past scandals. Trump has also called Paxton a “pain in the ass” and openly mocked his attire.

Paxton was recently reminded on Fox News about his many controversies, which included an indictment on security fraud charges in 2015, federal fraud charges in 2016 and accusations from staff members in 2020 of accepting bribes.

Despite all this, a recent Fox News survey shows Paxton is only tied with Democratic opponent James Talarico in the race.

Reuters last week reported that outside groups have spent $239 million to back Paxton in his race against Talarico, whom Trump has tried to insult by falsely calling him a vegan — with one particularly disturbing instance Tuesday.

“I mean, we shouldn’t be spending $200 million or $300 million in Texas to defend a Senate candidate,” McDaniel told Garrett. “So, there is a lot at stake. I think the House, with three seats that the Dems need to pick up, is probably going to go to the Democrats.”

She concluded, “And right now, all eyes are on the Senate, but certainly the map has expanded and Democrats are feeling bullish. And what I have seen is Republicans are turning out … which is encouraging for keeping the Senate.”
